brief: Exterior of the same house: rural Japanese house, abandoned for 5 years after a murder.
design_notes: Type: a one-story rural minka-style house. Post-and-beam frame, raised wooden floor on a stone base, deep eaves, kawara tile gable roof, a narrow engawa veranda along the front.

Walls: the classic two-part split. Lower wainscot of charred cedar (yakisugi) vertical boards, upper panels of aged lime plaster (shikkui) between exposed posts. Dark lower half against a pale upper half gives a strong, recognisable silhouette even at night.
Openings: wooden lattice (koshi) windows and lattice sliding doors at the entrance. One door panel is left half-open onto a dark interior. That's the hook that pulls a player in.

Five years abandoned: roof ridge sagging, tiles missing and slipped, moss on the roof and the base of the walls, rain streaks running down the plaster, siding boards missing or broken, lattice bars snapped.

After the murder: one window was boarded up from outside with fresher planks. Someone tried to seal something in, or keep people out. The boards are less weathered than everything else, so they read as 'after'.
Palette: charcoal yakisugi, grey-brown sun-bleached cedar, off-white stained plaster, blue-grey tiles, grey stone, green-black moss.
